claim: Direct interaction between egg JUNO and sperm IZUMO1 mediates gamete membrane adhesion in mammals.
source: In mammals, direct interaction between egg JUNO and sperm IZUMO1 mediates gamete membrane adhesion, yet their role in fusion remains enigmatic.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research establishing the JUNO-IZUMO1 interaction.

claim: The role of JUNO and IZUMO1 in fusion remains enigmatic.
source: In mammals, direct interaction between egg JUNO and sperm IZUMO1 mediates gamete membrane adhesion, yet their role in fusion remains enigmatic.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about the current state of knowledge regarding JUNO and IZUMO1 function.

claim: TMEM81 has structural homologies with both IZUMO1 and SPACA6.
source: We first identified TMEM81, whose gene is expressed by mouse and human spermatids, as a protein having structural homologies with both IZUMO1 and another sperm molecule essential for gamete fusion, SPACA6.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural prediction data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TMEM81 gene is expressed by mouse and human spermatids.
source: We first identified TMEM81, whose gene is expressed by mouse and human spermatids, as a protein having structural homologies with both IZUMO1 and another sperm molecule essential for gamete fusion, SPACA6.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to gene expression databases.

claim: A pentameric complex involving sperm IZUMO1, SPACA6, TMEM81 and egg JUNO, CD9 was identified using AlphaFold-Multimer predictions.
source: Using a set of proteins known to be important for fertilization and TMEM81, we then systematically searched for predicted binary interactions using an unguided approach and identified a pentameric complex involving sperm IZUMO1, SPACA6, TMEM81 and egg JUNO, CD9.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions presented in the manuscript.

claim: The pentameric complex is structurally consistent with the expected topology on opposing gamete membranes.
source: This complex is structurally consistent with both the expected topology on opposing gamete membranes and the location of predicted N-glycans not modeled by AlphaFold-Multimer, suggesting that its components could organize into a synapse-like assembly at the point of fusion.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of the predicted structure and biological knowledge.

claim: The pentameric complex is structurally consistent with the location of predicted N-glycans.
source: This complex is structurally consistent with both the expected topology on opposing gamete membranes and the location of predicted N-glycans not modeled by AlphaFold-Multimer, suggesting that its components could organize into a synapse-like assembly at the point of fusion.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of N-glycosylation sites in the predicted structure.

claim: The components of the pentameric complex could organize into a synapse-like assembly at the point of fusion.
source: This complex is structurally consistent with both the expected topology on opposing gamete membranes and the location of predicted N-glycans not modeled by AlphaFold-Multimer, suggesting that its components could organize into a synapse-like assembly at the point of fusion.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the structural predictions and biological context.

claim: Recognition between egg JUNO and sperm IZUMO1 is essential for the fusion of mouse gametes.
source: In particular, recognition between egg glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored protein JUNO and sperm type I transmembrane protein IZUMO1 was found to be essential for the fusion of mouse gametes by mediating the juxtaposition of their plasma membranes (Bianchi et al., 2014; Inoue et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior experimental studies.

claim: JUNO and IZUMO1 mediate the juxtaposition of gamete plasma membranes.
source: In particular, recognition between egg glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored protein JUNO and sperm type I transmembrane protein IZUMO1 was found to be essential for the fusion of mouse gametes by mediating the juxtaposition of their plasma membranes (Bianchi et al., 2014; Inoue et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior experimental studies.

claim: Neither JUNO nor IZUMO1 resembles known fusogens based on structural studies.
source: In agreement with such a docking function, structural studies showed that, although the architecture of the ectodomain of IZUMO1 is reminiscent of Plasmodium invasion proteins, neither molecule resembles known fusogens (Aydin et al., 2016; Han et al., 2016; Kato et al., 2016; Nishimura et al., 2016; Ohto et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The architecture of the ectodomain of IZUMO1 is reminiscent of Plasmodium invasion proteins.
source: In agreement with such a docking function, structural studies showed that, although the architecture of the ectodomain of IZUMO1 is reminiscent of Plasmodium invasion proteins, neither molecule resembles known fusogens (Aydin et al., 2016; Han et al., 2016; Kato et al., 2016; Nishimura et al., 2016; Ohto et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Mouse IZUMO1 was recently reported to have fusogenic activity in vitro.
source: at the same time, mouse IZUMO1 was recently reported to have fusogenic activity in vitro (Brukman et al., 2023), but whether this reflects a comparable function in vivo remains to be determined (Bianchi and Wright, 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Whether the in vitro fusogenic activity of mouse IZUMO1 reflects a comparable function in vivo remains to be determined.
source: at the same time, mouse IZUMO1 was recently reported to have fusogenic activity in vitro (Brukman et al., 2023), but whether this reflects a comparable function in vivo remains to be determined (Bianchi and Wright, 2023).
evidence: This is an explicit statement about uncertainty in the field, supported by citation.

claim: CD9 and CD81 are two phylogenetically close tetraspanin membrane proteins essential for mouse gamete fusion.
source: On the female side, these include two phylogenetically close tetraspanin membrane proteins, CD9 and CD81 (Miyado et al., 2000; Kaji et al., 2000; Miller et al., 2000; Rubinstein et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to gene ablation studies.

claim: CD9 concentrates to the gamete adhesion area concomitantly with IZUMO1.
source: CD9 concentrates to the gamete adhesion area concomitantly with IZUMO1 (Chalbi et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: CD9 is thought to facilitate fusion by reshaping the oocyte's plasma membrane.
source: CD9 concentrates to the gamete adhesion area concomitantly with IZUMO1 (Chalbi et al., 2014) and is thought to facilitate fusion by reshaping the oocyte's plasma membrane (Jégou et al., 2011; Umeda et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: CD81 is 44%-sequence identical to CD9.
source: CD81 is 44%-sequence identical to CD9 and can partially rescue the infertility of CD9-deficient mouse eggs (Kaji et al., 2002; Ohnami et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence comparison data cited from prior studies.

claim: CD81 can partially rescue the infertility of CD9-deficient mouse eggs.
source: CD81 is 44%-sequence identical to CD9 and can partially rescue the infertility of CD9-deficient mouse eggs (Kaji et al., 2002; Ohnami et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: SPACA6 is a type I-transmembrane protein with an IZUMO1-like ectodomain structure.
source: These include sperm acrosome membrane-associated protein 6 (SPACA6; Barbaux et al., 2020; Lamas-Toranzo et al., 2020; Lorenzetti et al., 2014; Noda et al., 2020) and transmembrane protein 95 (TMEM95; Lamas-Toranzo et al., 2020), both of which are type I-transmembrane proteins with an IZUMO1-like ectodomain structure (Lamas-Toranzo et al., 2020; Nishimura et al., 2016; Vance et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: TMEM95 is a type I-transmembrane protein with an IZUMO1-like ectodomain structure.
source: These include sperm acrosome membrane-associated protein 6 (SPACA6; Barbaux et al., 2020; Lamas-Toranzo et al., 2020; Lorenzetti et al., 2014; Noda et al., 2020) and transmembrane protein 95 (TMEM95; Lamas-Toranzo et al., 2020), both of which are type I-transmembrane proteins with an IZUMO1-like ectodomain structure (Lamas-Toranzo et al., 2020; Nishimura et al., 2016; Vance et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: DCST1 and DCST2 interact with each other.
source: Sperm dendrocyte expressed seven transmembrane protein domain-containing proteins 1 and 2 (DCST1/2), which interact with each other (Noda et al., 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: DCST1/2 are orthologues of molecules essential for fusion in worm (SPE-49/42) and fly (SNEAKY/DCST2).
source: Sperm dendrocyte expressed seven transmembrane protein domain-containing proteins 1 and 2 (DCST1/2), which interact with each other (Noda et al., 2022) and are orthologues of molecules essential for fusion in worm (SPE-49/42) (Kroft et al., 2005; Wilson et al., 2018) and fly (SNEAKY/DCST2) (Wilson et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies in other organisms.

claim: DCST1/2 are required for fertility in mouse and fish.
source: Sperm dendrocyte expressed seven transmembrane protein domain-containing proteins 1 and 2 (DCST1/2), which interact with each other (Noda et al., 2022) and are orthologues of molecules essential for fusion in worm (SPE-49/42) (Kroft et al., 2005; Wilson et al., 2018) and fly (SNEAKY/DCST2) (Wilson et al., 2006), are required for fertility not only in the mouse but also in fish (Inoue et al., 2021; Noda et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: FIMP is the transmembrane domain-containing isoform of 4930451I11RIK.
source: Finally, two other molecules necessary for mouse gamete fusion are fertilization influencing membrane protein (FIMP), the transmembrane domain-containing isoform of 4930451I11RIK (Fujihara et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: FIMP is necessary for mouse gamete fusion.
source: Finally, two other molecules necessary for mouse gamete fusion are fertilization influencing membrane protein (FIMP), the transmembrane domain-containing isoform of 4930451I11RIK (Fujihara et al., 2020), and sperm-oocyte fusion required 1 (SOF1; Noda et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: SOF1 is necessary for mouse gamete fusion.
source: Finally, two other molecules necessary for mouse gamete fusion are fertilization influencing membrane protein (FIMP), the transmembrane domain-containing isoform of 4930451I11RIK (Fujihara et al., 2020), and sperm-oocyte fusion required 1 (SOF1; Noda et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: IZUMO1 is part of rodent sperm multiprotein complexes that include structurally related molecules IZUMO2-4.
source: In addition to this gene knockout-derived information, there is biochemical evidence that IZUMO1 is part of rodent sperm multiprotein complexes that include structurally related molecules IZUMO2-4 (Ellerman et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a biochemical study.

claim: Egg FCRL3/MAIA was suggested to be involved in human gamete adhesion and fusion by replacing JUNO as an IZUMO1-binding partner.
source: More recently, egg Fc receptor-like 3 (FCRL3/MAIA) was also suggested to be involved in human gamete adhesion and fusion by replacing JUNO as an IZUMO1-binding partner (Vondrakova et al., 2022), although others have not confirmed this (Bianchi et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The role of FCRL3/MAIA in human gamete adhesion and fusion has not been confirmed by others.
source: More recently, egg Fc receptor-like 3 (FCRL3/MAIA) was also suggested to be involved in human gamete adhesion and fusion by replacing JUNO as an IZUMO1-binding partner (Vondrakova et al., 2022), although others have not confirmed this (Bianchi et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study that failed to confirm the original finding.

claim: A larger macromolecular complex may orchestrate mammalian egg-sperm fusion.
source: The relatively large number of proteins that these studies collectively identified as required for mammalian egg-sperm fusion, together with the lack of conclusive evidence supporting a direct role of the JUNO/IZUMO1 complex in the fusion process itself, suggest that — in line with the concept of fertilization synapse (Krauchunas et al., 2016) — a larger macromolecular complex may orchestrate fusion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the number of proteins required for fusion and the concept of fertilization synapse.

claim: The identification of additional protein-protein interactions between egg-sperm fusion factors has frustrated independent efforts by multiple laboratories.
source: However, perhaps because such an assembly exists only transiently due to the need to prevent polyspermy, the identification of additional protein-protein interactions between the aforementioned factors has frustrated independent efforts by multiple laboratories.
evidence: This is a statement about the difficulty of experimental detection, with speculation about the reason.

claim: The fusion synapse assembly may exist only transiently due to the need to prevent polyspermy.
source: However, perhaps because such an assembly exists only transiently due to the need to prevent polyspermy, the identification of additional protein-protein interactions between the aforementioned factors has frustrated independent efforts by multiple laboratories.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the difficulty in detecting protein complexes.

claim: Mouse JUNO and IZUMO1 components have such a low affinity that they cannot be purified as a stable complex, unlike their human homologs.
source: Here, we show that, despite the clear centrality of the JUNO/IZUMO1 interaction, its mouse components have such a low affinity that, unlike their human homologs, they cannot be purified as a stable complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The biochemical identification of other egg/sperm fusion factor complexes may be hindered by the fact that their binary affinities vary significantly among different species.
source: Because the biochemical identification of other egg/sperm fusion factor complexes may be hindered by the fact that their binary affinities also vary significantly among different species, we attack the problem by taking advantage of the momentous advances in protein complex structure prediction using AlphaFold-Multimer (Burke et al., 2023; Evans et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation about mouse vs. human JUNO/IZUMO1 affinity.

claim: The availability of a significant number of sequences for proteins of interest allows AlphaFold to predict possible complexes highly accurately.
source: The rationale for using this approach lies in the fact that the availability of a significant number of sequences for the proteins of interest not only allows AlphaFold to predict possible complexes thereof highly accurately (Jumper et al., 2021; Lee et al., 2023; Mirdita et al., 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to AlphaFold methodology papers.

claim: AlphaFold is largely insensitive to the species-specific affinity of a given protein-protein interaction.
source: The rationale for using this approach lies in the fact that the availability of a significant number of sequences for the proteins of interest not only allows AlphaFold to predict possible complexes thereof highly accurately (Jumper et al., 2021; Lee et al., 2023; Mirdita et al., 2022), but also makes it largely insensitive to the species-specific affinity of a given protein-protein interaction.
evidence: This is an inference about AlphaFold's properties based on its methodology.

claim: The analysis of AlphaFold-Multimer predictions supports the suggestion that JUNO and IZUMO1 are part of a complex that includes additional fusion factors.
source: Consistent with these considerations, the analysis of AlphaFold-Multimer predictions supports the suggestion that JUNO and IZUMO1 are part of a complex that includes additional fusion factors.
evidence: This claim is supported by the computational predictions presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mammalian cell-expressed human JUNO and IZUMO1 ectodomains form a stable complex that can be detected by size-exclusion chromatography.
source: Whereas mammalian cell-expressed human JUNO and IZUMO1 ectodomains form a stable complex (JUNOE/IZUMO1E) that can be detected by size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), their murine homologs do not (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Murine JUNO and IZUMO1 ectodomains do not form a stable complex that can be detected by size-exclusion chromatography.
source: Whereas mammalian cell-expressed human JUNO and IZUMO1 ectodomains form a stable complex (JUNOE/IZUMO1E) that can be detected by size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), their murine homologs do not (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The KD of mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E is 0.6–12 µM.
source: This is consistent with the low affinity of the interaction between the mouse proteins, whose 0.6–12 µM KD is significantly higher than the ~50–90 nM KD reported for the human JUNOE/IZUMO1E complex expressed in insect cells (Aydin et al., 2016; Bianchi et al., 2014; Nishimura et al., 2016; Ohto et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies measuring binding affinity.

claim: The KD of human JUNOE/IZUMO1E complex expressed in insect cells is ~50–90 nM.
source: This is consistent with the low affinity of the interaction between the mouse proteins, whose 0.6–12 µM KD is significantly higher than the ~50–90 nM KD reported for the human JUNOE/IZUMO1E complex expressed in insect cells (Aydin et al., 2016; Bianchi et al., 2014; Nishimura et al., 2016; Ohto et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies measuring binding affinity.

claim: The KD of wild-type mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E is higher than the 360 nM KD of the complex between human IZUMO1E and JUNOE W62A.
source: Notably, the KD of wild-type mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E is also higher than the 360 nM KD of the complex between human IZUMO1E and JUNOE W62A (Aydin et al., 2016; Ohto et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies measuring binding affinity.

claim: Introduction of the W62A mutation into mouse JUNO abolishes its ability to rescue the sperm-fusion impairment of Juno null eggs.
source: The latter bears an interface mutation whose introduction into mouse JUNO abolishes its ability to rescue the sperm-fusion impairment of Juno null eggs, as well as halves its ability to support sperm binding to JUNO-expressing human embryonic kidney 293T (HEK293T) cells (Kato et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: Introduction of the W62A mutation into mouse JUNO halves its ability to support sperm binding to JUNO-expressing HEK293T cells.
source: The latter bears an interface mutation whose introduction into mouse JUNO abolishes its ability to rescue the sperm-fusion impairment of Juno null eggs, as well as halves its ability to support sperm binding to JUNO-expressing human embryonic kidney 293T (HEK293T) cells (Kato et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: The low affinity of mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E could be partially compensated by the avidity resulting from a high local concentration of receptors at the egg/sperm contact point.
source: The low affinity of mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E could, in principle, be partially compensated by the avidity resulting from a high local concentration of receptors at the egg/sperm contact point.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for how low affinity interactions could still be functional.

claim: The binary interaction between JUNO and IZUMO1 may be stabilized within the context of a larger macromolecular complex.
source: At the same time, consistent with the considerations made above, the binary interaction between JUNO and IZUMO1 may be stabilized within the context of a larger macromolecular complex.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the observations about affinity and complex formation.

claim: AlphaFold-Multimer generates a high-confidence model of human JUNOE/IZUMO1E that accurately reproduces the corresponding crystal structure.
source: This computational experiment showed that AlphaFold-Multimer not only generates a high-confidence model of human JUNOE/IZUMO1E that accurately reproduces the corresponding crystal structure but also yields a model of mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E of comparable confidence (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 2.

claim: AlphaFold-Multimer yields a model of mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E of comparable confidence to the human complex.
source: This computational experiment showed that AlphaFold-Multimer not only generates a high-confidence model of human JUNOE/IZUMO1E that accurately reproduces the corresponding crystal structure but also yields a model of mouse JUNOE/IZUMO1E of comparable confidence (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 2.

claim: As long as a significant number of sequences can be aligned to those of a protein complex of interest and the interaction is evolutionarily conserved, the quality of AlphaFold-Multimer predictions is not negatively affected by the low affinity that its components may have in a subset of species.
source: This is consistent with the expectation that, as long as a significant number of sequences can be aligned to those of a protein complex of interest and the interaction is evolutionarily conserved, the quality of the AlphaFold-Multimer predictions for this complex is not negatively affected by the low affinity that its components may have in a subset of species.
evidence: This is an inference about AlphaFold's properties based on the computational results.

claim: TMEM81 is a clear structural homolog of the conserved immunoglobulin-like domain of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 based on Foldseek search.
source: Despite insignificant sequence identities (16–27%), this search also identified transmembrane protein 81 (TMEM81) as a clear structural homolog of the conserved immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domain of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 (E-values 1.40e-8–1.39e-6; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Foldseek search results and structural analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: TMEM81 has insignificant sequence identity (16–27%) with IZUMO1 and SPACA6.
source: Despite insignificant sequence identities (16–27%), this search also identified transmembrane protein 81 (TMEM81) as a clear structural homolog of the conserved immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domain of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 (E-values 1.40e-8–1.39e-6; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence comparison data.

claim: An AlphaFold model of TMEM81 ectodomain matched the crystal structure of human IZUMO1 with a Dali Z-score of 13.0.
source: The TMEM81 hit was confirmed by the result of a search of the PDB database, carried out by generating an AlphaFold model of the protein's ectodomain residues A31-N184 (average pLDDT 93.8) and using it as input for Dali (Holm, 2020), which matched it to the crystal structure of human IZUMO1 (PDB 5JK9; Ohto et al., 2016) with a Z-score of 13.0 (significantly above the Z-score threshold of 8, which indicates very good structural superpositions Holm, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by Dali search results using an AlphaFold model.

claim: A Dali Z-score above 8 indicates very good structural superpositions.
source: The TMEM81 hit was confirmed by the result of a search of the PDB database, carried out by generating an AlphaFold model of the protein's ectodomain residues A31-N184 (average pLDDT 93.8) and using it as input for Dali (Holm, 2020), which matched it to the crystal structure of human IZUMO1 (PDB 5JK9; Ohto et al., 2016) with a Z-score of 13.0 (significantly above the Z-score threshold of 8, which indicates very good structural superpositions Holm, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the Dali methodology.

claim: TMEM81 is conserved in vertebrates.
source: Notably, TMEM81 is conserved in vertebrates (NCBI, 2022), and its gene is expressed in both mouse and human spermatids (Jung et al., 2019; Uhlén et al., 2015; Yue et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to database and expression studies.

claim: TMEM81 is predicted to be a type I transmembrane protein with a large extracellular domain.
source: Like IZUMO1-3, SPACA6, and TMEM95, TMEM81 is predicted to be a type I transmembrane protein with a large extracellular domain
evidence: This claim is based on computational prediction of protein topology.

claim: TMEM81 was previously anonymously suggested to be a β-sheet-rich molecule that may be structurally related to IZUMO1.
source: moreover, it was previously anonymously suggested to be a β-sheet-rich molecule that may be structurally related to IZUMO1 (Wikipedia, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a Wikipedia entry.

claim: The characteristic four-helix bundle of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 is replaced by a three-stranded β-sheet in the AlphaFold model of TMEM81.
source: Accordingly, the characteristic four-helix bundle (4HB) of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 is replaced by a three-stranded β-sheet in the AlphaFold model of TMEM81
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis of AlphaFold models shown in Figure 3.

claim: The positioning of two invariant disulfide bonds that orient variable elements relative to the conserved Ig-like domain is remarkably similar in IZUMO1, SPACA6, and TMEM81.
source: however, the positioning of two invariant disulfide bonds that orient these highly different elements relative to the conserved Ig-like domain is remarkably similar in the three molecules (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: AlphaFold-Multimer was used to examine all pairwise interactions of the human homologs of 4 egg and 11 sperm proteins, including TMEM81, amounting to 120 unique combinations.
source: To infer whether a larger macromolecular complex may be involved in gamete fusion without introducing a large number of possible false positives (as observed in attempts to perform a large-scale screening), we used AlphaFold-Multimer in template-free mode to examine all pairwise interactions of the human homologs of the 4 egg and 11 sperm proteins mentioned above, including TMEM81. Since we also considered the possibility that each of these 15 different molecules may also homodimerize, this amounted to a total of 120 unique combinations.
evidence: This describes the computational approach used in the study.

claim: A cluster of 7 possible interactions centered around IZUMO1 was identified, 5 of which were direct (JUNO, CD9, CD81, SPACA6, TMEM81) and 2 indirect (IZUMO4 via JUNO, SOF1 via SPACA6).
source: Analysis of the corresponding predictions revealed a cluster of 7 possible interactions centered around IZUMO1, 5 of which were direct (JUNO, CD9, CD81, SPACA6, TMEM81) and 2 indirect (IZUMO4 (via JUNO), SOF1 (via SPACA6)).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 4.

claim: Isolated homodimeric interactions were detected for IZUMO4 and DCST1.
source: In addition, we detected isolated homodimeric interactions for IZUMO4 and DCST1, as well as heterodimeric interactions for IZUMO2/IZUMO3, TMEM95/FIMP and DCST1/DCST2 (Figure 4 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 4.

claim: Heterodimeric interactions were detected for IZUMO2/IZUMO3, TMEM95/FIMP and DCST1/DCST2.
source: In addition, we detected isolated homodimeric interactions for IZUMO4 and DCST1, as well as heterodimeric interactions for IZUMO2/IZUMO3, TMEM95/FIMP and DCST1/DCST2 (Figure 4 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 4.

claim: The ~260 Å-long mace-shaped heterodimeric assembly predicted for DCST1/DCST2 is consistent with experimental evidence for interaction between the two proteins.
source: Notably, the ~260 Å-long mace-shaped heterodimeric assembly predicted for DCST1/DCST2 is consistent with experimental evidence for interaction between the two proteins (Noda et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions and citation to experimental evidence.

claim: The two egg tetraspanins CD9 and CD81 are predicted to bind to the same region of IZUMO1 and are interchangeable.
source: Analysis of the resulting predictions (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), as well as the predictions of the binary complexes IZUMO1/CD9 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) or IZUMO1/CD81 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggest that the two egg tetraspanins are interchangeable because they are predicted to bind to the same region of IZUMO1
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 5 and supplements.

claim: IZUMO1 consistently interacts with CD9 when modeled together with both CD9 and CD81, in agreement with the observation that mouse fertility depends more on CD9 than CD81.
source: moreover, in agreement with the observation that mouse fertility depends more on CD9 than CD81 (Kaji et al., 2002; Kaji et al., 2000; Miller et al., 2000; Miyado et al., 2000; Ohnami et al., 2012; Rubinstein et al., 2006), IZUMO1 consistently interacts with the former when modeled together with both tetraspanins.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions and citations to experimental studies.

claim: IZUMO4 does not interact with the rest of the 8-protein complex assembly.
source: The 8-protein complex predictions also indicate that IZUMO4 does not interact with the rest of the assembly (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), consistent with the observation that its predicted binary interaction with JUNO (Figure 4) is incompatible with the JUNO/IZUMO1 interface (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 5.

claim: The predicted binary interaction between IZUMO4 and JUNO is incompatible with the JUNO/IZUMO1 interface.
source: The 8-protein complex predictions also indicate that IZUMO4 does not interact with the rest of the assembly (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), consistent with the observation that its predicted binary interaction with JUNO (Figure 4) is incompatible with the JUNO/IZUMO1 interface (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 5.

claim: SOF1 is mainly disordered and does not make significant contacts with other components of the 8-protein complex.
source: Finally, pDockQ and visual analysis of the predictions for the 8-protein complex indicate that SOF1 is mainly disordered and does not make significant contacts with other components (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 5.

claim: A 5-protein complex consisting of egg JUNO and CD9 and sperm IZUMO1, SPACA6 and TMEM81 can be consistently modeled with acceptable ranking confidence and pDockQ scores.
source: Taken together, these considerations leave egg JUNO and CD9 and sperm IZUMO1, SPACA6 and TMEM81 as subunits of a 5-protein complex that can be consistently modeled with acceptable ranking confidence and pDockQ scores (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions shown in Figure 5.

claim: JUNO and IZUMO1 constitute the core of the putative 5-protein assembly and interact in the same way that was observed crystallographically.
source: Consistent with their central role in interfacing the egg and sperm plasma membranes, JUNO and IZUMO1 constitute the core of this putative assembly, where they interact in the same way that was observed crystallographically (Aydin et al., 2016; Ohto et al., 2016) and reproduced computationally (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions and citations to crystal structures.

claim: The hinge region and 4HB of SPACA6 wrap around the 4HB of IZUMO1, generating a concave surface that interacts with the LEL of CD9.
source: On the opposite side of the JUNO/IZUMO1 interface, the hinge region and 4HB of SPACA6 wrap around the 4HB of IZUMO1, generating a concave surface that interacts with the long extracellular loop (LEL) of CD9.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis of the predicted complex shown in Figure 5.

claim: TMEM81 adopts the same N-to-C orientation of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 and links their C-terminal regions by inserting its Ig-like module between the two proteins.
source: Finally, TMEM81 adopts the same N-to-C orientation of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 and, by inserting its Ig-like module between the two proteins, links their C-terminal regions.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis of the predicted complex shown in Figure 5.

claim: The C-termini of egg subunits or the egg subunits themselves should all be located on the opposite side of the corresponding elements from sperm, relative to the gamete interface, in a gamete fusion synapse.
source: Firstly, because the majority of proteins involved in this process are either C-terminally membrane-anchored or transmembrane proteins, a basic feature expected in a gamete fusion synapse is that the C-termini of its egg subunits or the egg subunits themselves should all be located on the opposite side of the corresponding elements from sperm, relative to the gamete interface.
evidence: This is an inference based on biological knowledge about membrane protein topology.

claim: The 5-component complex predictions satisfy the expected topology on opposing gamete membranes.
source: This is true for the 5-component complex predictions (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of the predicted structure shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The predicted complex architecture is compatible with the location of all the possible N-glycosylation sites of JUNO, IZUMO1, SPACA6, and TMEM81, for both human and mouse homologs.
source: As shown in Figure 6, the predicted complex architecture is compatible with the location of all the possible N-glycosylation sites of JUNO, IZUMO1, SPACA6, and TMEM81, for both human and mouse homologs (amounting to a total of 10 sites).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: A sequon within the short extracellular loop of CD9 is conserved in both human and mouse species (corresponding to human N52 and mouse N50, respectively) but its glycosylation remains to be experimentally verified.
source: One possible exception is a sequon within the short extracellular loop (SEL) of CD9, which is conserved in both species (corresponding to human N52 and mouse N50, respectively) but whose glycosylation remains to be experimentally verified.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence analysis and notes the lack of experimental verification.

claim: If the conserved sequon of CD9 is glycosylated, this may interfere with the only minor contact that CD9 makes with JUNO within the predicted complex.
source: This suggests that if the conserved sequon of CD9 is glycosylated, this may interfere with the only minor contact that the protein makes with JUNO within the predicted complex.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the structural analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: A fusion synapse architecture where CD9 makes little or no contact with JUNO but interacts with the 4HB of IZUMO would explain the experimental observation that CD9 is recruited to the gamete fusion site only upon binding of JUNO to IZUMO1 in mouse oocytes.
source: Notably, a fusion synapse architecture where CD9 makes little or no contact with JUNO but interacts with the 4HB of IZUMO would immediately explain the experimental observation that, in mouse oocytes, CD9 is recruited to the gamete fusion site only upon binding of JUNO to IZUMO1 (Chalbi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference that connects the predicted structure to experimental observations.

claim: The predicted CD9/IZUMO1 interface agrees with previous suggestions that the two proteins may interact, based on the observation that their sequences co-evolve.
source: Moreover, the predicted CD9/IZUMO1 interface agrees with previous suggestions that the two proteins may interact, based on the observation that their sequences co-evolve (Claw et al., 2014; Vicens and Roldan, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by computational predictions and citations to co-evolution studies.

claim: The conserved CD9 Phe at the center of the SFQ tripeptide (175-TFT-177 in human) stacks against α-helix 2 of the IZUMO 4HB in the predictions.
source: Against this background, it is interesting to note that, in our predictions, the conserved CD9 Phe at the center of the SFQ tripeptide (175-TFT-177 in human) stacks against α-helix 2 of the IZUMO 4HB (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The third α-helix of CD9 LEL makes hydrophobic contacts with IZUMO1 α2 and α4 in the predictions.
source: Not far from this interaction, the third α-helix of CD9 LEL makes hydrophobic contacts with IZUMO1 α2 and α4.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: L115 is a conserved IZUMO1 α4 residue thought to contribute to egg binding and fusion.
source: These interactions are close to L115, a conserved IZUMO1 α4 residue thought to contribute to egg binding and fusion (Inoue et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: W113 is a conserved IZUMO1 α4 amino acid that was recently implicated in fusion.
source: These interactions are close to L115, a conserved IZUMO1 α4 residue thought to contribute to egg binding and fusion (Inoue et al., 2013), and directly involve W113, another conserved α4 amino acid that was recently implicated in fusion (Brukman et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: W113 bridges CD9 and SPACA6 by inserting between their LEL and double CXXC motif elements, respectively, in the predictions.
source: Notably, W113 bridges CD9 and SPACA6 by inserting between their LEL and double CXXC motif elements, respectively, while W88 — another IZUMO1 residue suggested to be important for fusion (Brukman et al., 2023) — also interacts hydrophobically with SPACA6 at the opposite side of IZUMO1's 4HB (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: W88 is another IZUMO1 residue suggested to be important for fusion that interacts hydrophobically with SPACA6 at the opposite side of IZUMO1's 4HB in the predictions.
source: Notably, W113 bridges CD9 and SPACA6 by inserting between their LEL and double CXXC motif elements, respectively, while W88 — another IZUMO1 residue suggested to be important for fusion (Brukman et al., 2023) — also interacts hydrophobically with SPACA6 at the opposite side of IZUMO1's 4HB (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 7B and citation.

claim: Despite the fact that IZUMO1 complementation rescues the disappearance of SPACA6 from the mature sperm of IZUMO1 null mice, attempts to biochemically identify a complex between IZUMO1 and SPACA6 have been met with limited success.
source: First, it remains unclear why, despite the fact that IZUMO1 complementation rescues the disappearance of SPACA6 from the mature sperm of IZUMO1 null mice (Inoue et al., 2021), attempts to biochemically identify a complex between IZUMO1 and SPACA6 have been met with limited success (Noda et al., 2020; Vance et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: In order to be stable, the interaction between IZUMO1 and SPACA6 may require the presence of TMEM81.
source: Based on the predicted complex architecture, one obvious possibility would be that, in order to be stable, the interaction also requires the presence of TMEM81.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation based on the predicted complex structure.

claim: The low affinity of the interactions between IZUMO1, SPACA6, and TMEM81 is typical of extracellular receptor-ligand interactions and makes them difficult to detect experimentally.
source: One reason could be the low affinity of the interactions between these proteins, which is typical of extracellular receptor-ligand interactions and makes them difficult to detect experimentally (Wright and Bianchi, 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on general knowledge about receptor-ligand interactions, supported by citation.

claim: To avoid any inappropriate membrane fusion events, the individual components of the complex may be purposefully spatially segregated until brought together at the moment of fusion.
source: Also, to avoid any inappropriate membrane fusion events, the individual components of the complex may be purposefully spatially segregated until brought together at the moment of fusion, again making it difficult to detect this complex in vivo.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the difficulty in detecting the complex.

claim: The structural modeling approach described could play a role in understanding the function of dynamic and transiently formed protein complexes in a range of biological processes that would otherwise be difficult to identify.
source: The type of structural modeling approach described here could play a role in understanding the function of dynamic and transiently formed protein complexes in a range of biological processes that would otherwise be difficult to identify, although care should be taken as some complexes might be predicted due to interactions between homologs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the broader applicability of the approach.

claim: It is difficult to assess the confidence of the interface between CD9 and IZUMO1+SPACA6 due to its relatively limited extent (combined interface area ~730 Å2).
source: Second, because it is difficult to assess the confidence of the interface between CD9 and IZUMO1+SPACA6 due to its relatively limited extent (combined interface area ~730 Å2), it cannot be excluded that some protein other than CD9 may be the true counterpart of IZUMO1+SPACA6.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about uncertainty in the predictions, based on interface area analysis.

claim: It cannot be excluded that some protein other than CD9 may be the true counterpart of IZUMO1+SPACA6.
source: Second, because it is difficult to assess the confidence of the interface between CD9 and IZUMO1+SPACA6 due to its relatively limited extent (combined interface area ~730 Å2), it cannot be excluded that some protein other than CD9 may be the true counterpart of IZUMO1+SPACA6.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about uncertainty in the predictions.

claim: AlphaFold-Multimer may recognize that the concave surface generated by the combined 4HBs of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 is likely to engage in additional interactions and thus tries to fill it with another suitable input subunit.
source: In other words, it is, in principle, also possible that AlphaFold-Multimer simply recognizes that the concave surface generated by the combined 4HBs of IZUMO1 and SPACA6 is likely to engage in additional interactions and thus tries to fill it with another suitable input subunit.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about how AlphaFold-Multimer may be generating predictions.

claim: An independent study submitted back to back with the original preprint of the present manuscript provides experimental data for the existence of a trimeric IZUMO1/SPACA6/TMEM81 complex in zebrafish.
source: Of direct relevance to these questions is an independent study, submitted back to back with the original preprint of the present manuscript, which provides experimental data for the existence of a trimeric IZUMO1/SPACA6/TMEM81 complex in zebrafish and suggests that this interacts with egg Bouncer (Deneke et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an independent study.

claim: The independent study suggests that the trimeric IZUMO1/SPACA6/TMEM81 complex interacts with egg Bouncer in zebrafish.
source: Of direct relevance to these questions is an independent study, submitted back to back with the original preprint of the present manuscript, which provides experimental data for the existence of a trimeric IZUMO1/SPACA6/TMEM81 complex in zebrafish and suggests that this interacts with egg Bouncer (Deneke et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an independent study.

claim: The mammalian orthologue of Bouncer is expressed on sperm instead of the egg.
source: Considering that the mammalian orthologue of Bouncer is expressed on sperm instead of the egg (Fujihara et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: The role of CD9 in egg-sperm fusion is much more important in mammals than in fish.
source: Considering that the mammalian orthologue of Bouncer is expressed on sperm instead of the egg (Fujihara et al., 2021) and that role of CD9 in egg-sperm fusion is much more important in mammals than in fish (Greaves et al., 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a comparative study.

claim: During the course of evolution, CD9 may have substituted Bouncer as a binding partner of the IZUMO1/SPACA6/TMEM81 complex.
source: Considering that the mammalian orthologue of Bouncer is expressed on sperm instead of the egg (Fujihara et al., 2021) and that role of CD9 in egg-sperm fusion is much more important in mammals than in fish (Greaves et al., 2022), the combination of our studies raises the intriguing possibility that, during the course of evolution, CD9 may have substituted Bouncer as a binding partner of the IZUMO1/SPACA6/TMEM81 complex.
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary hypothesis based on comparative data.
